metadata.title: Findings from the TIMSS 2019 Problem Solving and Inquiry Tasks

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document reports descriptive findings and task-level performance for TIMSS 2019 Problem Solving and Inquiry (PSI) tasks administered in eTIMSS (computer-based) and compared to eTIMSS achievement scales. The provided excerpt does not describe the use of TIMSS sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) for the reported percentages and scale-score comparisons. Because the manuscript section shown focuses on task design, completion rates, and percent-correct/percent-full-credit results (and includes an appendix on automated scoring), the weighting strategy is not explicitly documented in the text provided. Therefore, weighting cannot be confirmed from the excerpt; the analysis should be treated as not explicitly weight-documented in the supplied material.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report’s main reported outcomes are task-level percent correct/percent full credit and completion/non-response indicators for PSI items, rather than cognitive achievement outcomes expressed as TIMSS plausible values (PVs). PV handling is therefore not applicable to the primary task-level descriptive results presented in the excerpt. Missing-data handling is not reported as a formal imputation/deletion strategy for the PSI item-level percentages; instead, the report discusses TIMSS “not reached” treatment and uses timing/log information to interpret non-response, but does not specify a PV-based missing-data procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The excerpt indicates that PSI tasks were administered only in eTIMSS countries (computer-based assessment), with PSI blocks rotated across eBooklets (eBooklets 15–16) and students completing one booklet. The report treats “not reached” responses as “not administered” (i.e., excluded from percent-correct computations) and uses event-log timing to distinguish stopping behavior from running out of time. For the automated scoring appendix, response images were extracted from TIMSS 2019 Building PSI item MQ12B03 across 22 participating countries plus benchmarking participants, then split into training and validation samples by country.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 4 Mathematics (School Party PSI task)
main_findings.target_variable: School Party item performance (percent correct/full credit)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported as ML metrics; reported percent correct/full credit by country and gender (e.g., average 42% correct for Screen 2A; 65% correct for Screen 6A; 14% full credit for Screen 6B).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 4 Mathematics data, the report summarizes task performance (percent correct/full credit) for the School Party PSI task across countries and by gender, finding substantial cross-country variation and generally higher boys’ performance on several screens; no predictive ML model is used for these descriptive task-level outcomes. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 4 Science (Farm Investigation PSI task)
main_findings.target_variable: Farm Investigation item performance (percent correct/full credit)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported as ML metrics; reported percent correct/full credit by country and gender (e.g., 25% full credit on Screen 2; 45% correct on Screen 3; 54% correct on Screen 6).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 4 Science data, the report summarizes task performance for the Farm Investigation PSI task across countries and by gender, finding that inquiry-practice items (measurement/data-collection) often show higher success than items requiring more complex reasoning or explanations. This indicates that  for the Farm Investigation PSI task across countries and by gender, finding that inquiry-practice items (measurement/data-collection) often show higher success than items requiring more complex reasoning or explanations.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 8 Mathematics (Building PSI task)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported as ML metrics; reported percent correct/full credit by country and gender (e.g., 69% correct for Screen 2; 23% correct for Screen 3; 26% full credit for Screen 4).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 8 Mathematics data, the report summarizes Building PSI task performance across countries and by gender, finding moderate success on early construction steps and lower success on later reasoning-heavy steps, with limited gender differences overall. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 8 Science (Pepper Plants PSI task)
main_findings.target_variable: Pepper Plants item performance (percent correct/full credit)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported as ML metrics; reported percent correct/full credit by country and gender (e.g., 78% correct for Screen 1; 27% correct for Screen 3; 43% full credit for Screen 4).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 eTIMSS Grade 8 Science data, the report summarizes Pepper Plants PSI task performance across countries and by gender, finding that students show reasonable understanding of fair-test concepts but weaker understanding of effective experimental controls, with notable cross-country variation. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 Building PSI (MQ12B03) response images (automated scoring study)
main_findings.target_variable: Automated classification of response-image score category
main_findings.performance_metrics: Feedforward neural network (FFN) in R/Keras: validation accuracy 90.35%; full-credit accuracy 94.74%; incorrect accuracy 89.56%; partial-credit accuracy 66.18%.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 Building PSI response-image the study leveraged a feedforward neural network to classify responses into score categories, finding high overall validation accuracy (90.35%) and strong performance for full-credit and incorrect images, but lower accuracy for partial-credit images (66.18%). The study is an automated scoring feasibility test rather than a causal model; it does not incorporate survey weights in the excerpt and uses a train/validation split by country. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2019 report documents task-level performance and non-response patterns for four PSI tasks administered in eTIMSS: School Party (Grade 4 Math), Farm Investigation (Grade 4 Science), Building (Grade 8 Math), and Pepper Plants (Grade 8 Science). Across tasks, the report reports percent-correct/percent-full-credit and completion/non-response rates by country and gender, showing substantial cross-country variation and generally small-to-moderate gender differences depending on the screen. For the only explicit ML component, the automated scoring appendix trains a feedforward neural network (FFN) in R/Keras on Building PSI response images, achieving 90.35% validation accuracy overall, with 94.74% accuracy for full-credit and 89.56% for incorrect responses, but only 66.18% for partial credit. The excerpt does not provide a PV-based modeling framework for these descriptive outcomes, and it does not document a formal missing-data imputation strategy beyond TIMSS “not reached” treatment and timing/log-based interpretation.
